subject: no variation in the values of the parameters within the chains

messages.author: 64e46511fd071141
messages.subject: no variation in the values of the parameters within the chains
parts:
Hello, 
I am fitting a non-homogeneous poisson process to a population of documents, where each document is represented by a vector of times at which it is cited (time since publication).
The full non-homogeneous poisson process has 3 parameters for each document, but for the time being I'm fixing two of them at some estimated average value for the population and trying to make sure I obtain reasonable inferences for the third parameter, named l.
I simulated the process to obtain fake data. For each simulated vector, I sampled from Gamma(1.2,1.25). Below is my Stan code to see if I recover the lambda value of each document in the simplest case where I specify the exact prior for l (in the real case, I will have hyperparameters and learn the distribution of lambda from the data) and the other parameters are fixed and equal across cases. 
The problem is that the parameters in the chains I obtain are invariant from one iteration to the next (but different across the chains), as if no sampling was happening. This seems to be the case also in the warmup part. I plotted the neg log-likelihood function for a number of these simulated observations and it looked fine (single minimum around the right value, nice curvature -- but might I have written it wrong in Stan?), so I don't understand what explains this behavior. 
This is probably a silly mistake, and I would appreciate your help. 
My code is below: 

imp_code = """
data {
int<lower=0> NNd; // total number of citation events
int<lower=0> N; // total number of documents
int<lower=0> Nd[N]; // number of citation events of each document
int<lower=0> Ts[N]; // length ( days) of the period of observation of each document
vector[NNd] y; // citation events
}
transformed data {
int<lower=0> m;
real<lower=0> mu; // location of the lognormal decay function
real<lower=0> s; // scale of the lognormal decay function
m <- 3;
mu <- 7.38;/
s <-1.2; 
}
parameters {
real<lower=0> l[N]; // importance parameter for each case
}
model {
int pos;
pos <- 1;
for (n in 1:N) {
    l[n] ~ gamma(1.2,1/.8);
    segment(y, pos,Nd[n]) ~ lognormal(mu,s); 
    increment_log_prob(l[n]*normal_cdf((log(segment(y,pos,Nd[n]))-mu)/s,0,1));
    increment_log_prob(-l[n]*(Nd[n]+m)*normal_cdf((log(Ts[n])-mu)/s,0,1));
    increment_log_prob(l[n]^Nd[n]);
    pos <- pos + Nd[n];    
}
}"""

netdata = {'NNd':sum(Nd),'N':len(Nd),'Nd':Nd,'Ts':Ts,'y':y} # Nd is a vector giving the number of citations for each case -- fake data simulated drawing from l ~ Gamma(1.2,1/.8) and mu = 3, s = 1.2.
netmodel = StanModel(model_code = imp_code)
fit = netmodel.sampling( data = netdata, iter = 10000, chains = 3, thin = 1, warmup = 5000)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] no variation in the values of the parameters within the chains
parts:
I don't know the model you're trying to fit (as in can't
verify the actual density), but I think you're trying to
increment with the density, not the log density. For
example, you probably want normal_cdf_log.

Also, I'm guessing you can vectorize this, especially
if Nd[n] just moves along

> for (n in 1:N) {
> l[n] ~ gamma(1.2,1/.8);
> segment(y, pos,Nd[n]) ~ lognormal(mu,s);

with the much more efficient vectorized forms:

l ~ gamma(1.2, 1.25);
y ~ lognormal(mu, s);

Given that y, mu, and s are data, the lognormal will actually
be a no-op (but that's presumably what you're going to swap out
later).

- Bob
